references.text: God broke the yoke that bound Israel in Egypt; here He threatens to break their pride if they are disobedient.
The same curse: the sky becoming like bronze and the earth like iron, drought as punishment for disobedience.
Isaiah prophesies that human pride will be humbled and the Lord's greatness alone exalted.
Israel speaks in pride and arrogance, something God will crush.
Jeremiah speaks of how God will destroy Judah's and Jerusalem's great pride.
Ezekiel prophesies that God will put an end to the arrogance of the proud.
Egypt's mighty pride shall fall, parallel to the threat to break Israel's pride.
Solomon's prayer: when the heavens are shut up and there is no rain because of sin, may God forgive.
Amos describes how God withheld rain as punishment, fulfilling the curse.
Haggai describes drought over the land because the people neglected God's house, a similar punishment to that in Leviticus.
